section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single present study examining associations between nature exposure, connectedness to nature, and body appreciation in U.S. adult women and men, reporting that both exposure and connectedness are positively associated with body appreciation and that self-esteem mediates these relationships. The authors note some gender differences in mediation (additional appearance-related mediators in men), acknowledge reliance on self-report and cross-sectional/online recruitment limitations, and suggest future directions including experimental and broader-sample work.

section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes a single U.S. study reporting that both connectedness to nature and exposure to nature are positively associated with body appreciation in adult women and men, with self-esteem mediating these relationships for both genders. The authors note gender differences in mediation pathways (men additionally showed mediation via motivational salience of appearance and internalisation of a muscular ideal), highlight reliance on cross-sectional and self-reported online data, and recommend replication and broader-sample work.

section_summary.extract_value: The Discussion reports results from a single study of U.S. adult women and men examining associations between nature exposure, connectedness to nature, and body appreciation. Connectedness to nature and exposure to nature were positively associated with body appreciation, with self-esteem mediating these relationships in both genders and additional mediators (motivational salience and internalisation of a muscular ideal) evident in men. Limitations noted include cross-sectional design, self-reported measures, online recruitment, and a call for replication and extension in diverse samples.
